chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a medicine that was kneaded with wine. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by Allah, I do not like to look at it, so how can I cure myself with it? Indeed, it is in the status of the fat of the swine or the flesh of the swine, and indeed some people cure themselves with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on medicine mixed with wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the ruling on wine-mixed medicine from mere prohibition to a profound aversion, comparing it to pork to emphasize its spiritual and physical impurity even when used for healing. This hadith, found in the chapter on 'desperation' (darura), highlights the tension between medical necessity and ritual purity, noting that while people utilize it, the Imam’s personal dislike underscores its inferior status compared to pure alternatives. It serves as a key text in Shia jurisprudence for evaluating the permissibility of intoxicants in non-drinking contexts, particularly when no pure substitute is available.
